text.p: Brazilian club side Palmeiras beat the New England Revolution of the United States 1-0 in a friendly at Foxboro Stadium Wednesday.
Substitute Euller provided the only goal in a lackluster affair before a crowd of 19,623.
In the 70th minute, Galeano sent a high ball to the top of the New England box where Euller got past defender Brian Dunseth and headed past goalkeeper Scott Coufal who failed to punch the ball clear.

The goal marked one of only a handful of opportunities for the Sao Paulo-based side, which is preparing for Reebok Cup matches Friday against Atletico Junior (Colombia) in Miami and Sunday against Necaxa (Mexico) in Chicago.

Palmieras were content to play the brunt of the game at half pace while New England, currently third in Major League Soccer's Eastern Conference at 12-8, got a chance to use a number of second-choice players.

"This was really a scrimmage for us," Palmeiras coach Luiz Felipe Scolari said. "We will prepare more aggressively for the Reebok Cup. We played a different rhythm tonight, but it gave me the chance to look at some new players."
One of seven new players on the Palmeiras side was veteran midfielder Zinho, who came to the team on Monday from Yokohama of the J-League where he had been playing since the 1994 World Cup.

"I think this was a great opportunity for my guys," said Revolution coach Thomas Rongen. "Any time you get a chance to play a team of this calibre, it's exciting. Palmeiras is one of the strongest sides in the world."

The Brazilians had the better chances in the opening half. In the sixth minute, defender Junior shot high from 18 meters. At 31 minutes, Cleber set Junior free down the left side where he made a run unmolested before shooting directly at goalkeeper Coufal from seven meters.
U.S. international Alexi Lalas headed straigh at Veloso in the 13th minute and shot high from 12 meters in the 36th minute.

The Revolution's best chance came at 65 minutes when Darren Sawatzky's header of a Alberto Naveda free kick went just wide at the left post. In the final minute, New England's Alejandro Farias hit a 24-meter shot from the left side directly at Veloso.
The match marked the return of U.S. international Joe-Max Moore who made his first appearance in 10 games for New England. Moore had been sidelined since May 24.
MLS teams have won four, lost five and tied four against international competition this year.

New England - 27-Scott Coufal, 3-Erik Imler, 2-Brian Dunseth, 22-Alexi Lalas (20-Francis Okaroh, 46), 5-Ted Chronopolous (25-Alejandro Farias, 46) 6-Leonardo Squadrone (21-Rob Jachym, 46), 14-Sam George, 8-Imad Baba (7-Darren Sawatzky, 46), 16-Evans Wise, 10-Alberto Naveda, 9-John Kerr (Joe-Max Moore, 41).
